prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were in an accident — I can help you find the right lawyer, but first I need a few details. Briefly tell me:
- Where (ZIP or nearest city) in Pleasanton you are or where the accident happened.
- How serious your injuries are (treated on scene, ER visit, ongoing treatment, surgery).
- Whether fault is disputed or the other driver admitted fault.
- Whether the other driver or you have insurance, and whether the insurer has contacted you.
- Any other complications (government vehicle involved, DUI, pedestrian/bike, hit-and-run).

While you answer, here’s how to decide which lawyer to hire and what to do next.

Which lawyer to hire — key criteria
- Focus: pick an attorney who concentrates on car-accident/personal-injury cases (not a general practitioner).
- Experience & track record: look for experience with cases like yours (injury severity, liability issues, insurance disputes). Trial experience matters if your case might go to court.
- Local knowledge: a Bay Area/Alameda County lawyer who knows local courts, judges, and insurers is helpful.
- Communication and attention: ask who will actually handle the matter (owner, partner, associate) and how often you’ll get updates.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical splits: about 33% for pre-suit, up to ~40% if the case goes to trial; confirm costs and whether the firm advances litigation expenses.
- Reputation: check State Bar status, client reviews (Avvo, Google/Yelp), and peer-rated directories (Martindale-Hubbell).

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases do you handle per year? What percent of your practice is personal injury?
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the typical outcomes?
- Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? How will you communicate with me and how often?
- Do you have trial experience? Have you taken similar cases to verdict?
- What is your estimated range of recovery and timeline for my case?
- Can you provide references or recent settlements/verdicts (anonymized)?

Red flags to avoid
- No written fee agreement or unclear fee/costs.
- Pressuring you to accept a settlement too quickly.
- No trial experience and unwillingness to go to trial if needed.
- Poor reviews about communication or responsiveness.

Immediate steps you should take now
- Seek and continue medical care; document everything.
- Keep police report number and get a copy of the report.
- Preserve photos of the scene, your injuries, vehicle damage, and any video if available.
- Get insurer and other driver info; record witness names/contact info.
- Do not give a recorded statement to the other party’s insurer without talking to an attorney first.
- Save all bills, prescriptions, mileage, pay stubs (for lost wages), and correspondence.

Timelines and legal deadlines (California)
- Personal-injury statute of limitations: generally 2 years from the accident (California Code of Civil Procedure § 335.1).
- If a government vehicle or agency is involved, you may have much shorter notice/claim deadlines (often 6 months). Act quickly.

How I can help next
- If you give me your ZIP code and a little more about your injuries and situation, I can suggest a short list of well-reviewed Pleasanton/Tri-Valley Bay Area personal-injury lawyers and local lawyer-referral resources (State Bar referral, local bar association).
- Or I can draft a short message you can use when contacting attorneys to get the information you need from initial consultations.

Tell me your ZIP and a few facts about the accident/injuries and I’ll pull together a tailored list.
